title: Pauliteiros de Miranda
summary: A stick dance of the Miranda region of Portugal performed by men in skirts, with bagpipes and drums, in which the dancers strike sticks together in rhythm.
howToPlay: A row of dancers faces down a long hall; each pair of sticks stands behind a pillar, from the nearest to the farthest.
Strike the pair a closing ring marks, on the beat, and the sticks cross and clack together.
Keep a steady count: the clash runs up and down the row.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra stroke costs points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Eight dancers in skirts strike their sticks together in rhythm and perform clack-and-turn sequences, to the bagpipe and drums.
credits: Tradition: pauliteiros of Miranda do Douro; patterns written for this game
